# tempfile - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempfile/^3.2/

## Expand description

This is a library for creating temporary files and directories that are automatically deleted when no longer referenced (i.e., on drop).

- Use `tempfile()``std::fs::File`
- Use `NamedTempFile::new()`*named*temporary file that can be referred to its path.
- Use `tempdir()`
- Use `spooled_tempfile()`

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

This crate provides several approaches to creating temporary files and directories.
[ tempfile()](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) relies on the OS to remove the temporary file once the last handle is closed.

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`[both rely on Rust destructors for cleanup.](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[§](https://docs.rs#resource-leaking)Resource Leaking

`tempfile` will (almost) never fail to cleanup temporary resources. However `TempDir` and
`NamedTempFile` will fail if their destructors don’t run. This is because `tempfile` relies on
the OS to cleanup the underlying file, while `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on rust
destructors to do so. Destructors may fail to run if the process exits through an unhandled
signal interrupt (like `SIGINT`), or if the instance is declared statically (like with
[ lazy_static](https://github.com/rust-lang-nursery/lazy-static.rs/issues/62)), among other possible reasons.

[§](https://docs.rs#unexpected-file-deletion)Unexpected File Deletion

Most operating systems periodically clean up temporary files that haven’t been accessed recently
(often on the order of multiple days). This issue does not affect unnamed temporary files but
can invalidate the paths associated with named temporary files on Unix-like systems because the
temporary file can be unlinked from the filesystem while still open and in-use. See the
[temporary file cleaner](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners) section for more security implications.

[§](https://docs.rs#security)Security

This section discusses security issues relevant to Unix-like operating systems that use shared temporary directories by default. Importantly, it’s not relevant for Windows or macOS as both operating systems use private per-user temporary directories by default.

Applications can mitigate the issues described below by using [ env::override_temp_dir](https://docs.rs/env/fn.override_temp_dir.html) to
change the default temporary directory but should do so if and only if default the temporary
directory (

[) is unsuitable (is world readable, world writable, managed by a temporary file cleaner, etc.).](https://docs.rs/env/fn.temp_dir.html)

`env::temp_dir`[§](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners)Temporary File Cleaners

In the presence of pathological temporary file cleaner, relying on file paths is unsafe because a temporary file cleaner could delete the temporary file which an attacker could then replace.

This isn’t an issue for [ tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) as it doesn’t rely on file paths. However,

[and temporary directories](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`*do*rely on file paths for

*some*operations. See the security documentation on the

[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[types for more information.](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`Mitigation:

- This is rarely an issue for short-lived files as temporary file cleaners usually only remove temporary files that haven’t been modified or accessed within many (10-30) days.
- Very long lived temporary files should be placed in directories not managed by temporary file cleaners.

[§](https://docs.rs#access-permissions)Access Permissions

Temporary *files* created with this library are private by default on all operating systems.
However, temporary *directories* are created with the default permissions and will therefore be
world-readable by default unless the user has changed their umask and/or default temporary
directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#denial-of-service)Denial of Service

If the file-name randomness ([ Builder::rand_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.rand_bytes)) is too small and/or this crate is built
without the

`getrandom` feature, it may be possible for an attacker to predict the random file
names chosen by this library, preventing temporary file creation by creating temporary files
with these predicted file names. By default, this library mitigates this denial of service
attack by:- Defaulting to 6 random characters per temporary file forcing an attacker to create billions of files before random collisions are expected (at which point you probably have larger problems).
- Re-seeding the random filename generator from system randomness after 3 failed attempts to
create temporary a file (when the `getrandom`feature is enabled as it is by default on all major platforms).

[§](https://docs.rs#early-drop-pitfall)Early drop pitfall

Because `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on their destructors for cleanup, this can lead
to an unexpected early removal of the directory/file, usually when working with APIs which are
generic over `AsRef<Path>`. Consider the following example:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::process::Command;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let temp_dir = tempdir()?;
// Spawn the `touch` command inside the temporary directory and collect the exit status
// Note that `temp_dir` is **not** moved into `current_dir`, but passed as a reference
let exit_status = Command::new("touch").arg("tmp").current_dir(&temp_dir).status()?;
assert!(exit_status.success());
```
This works because a reference to `temp_dir` is passed to `current_dir`, resulting in the
destructor of `temp_dir` being run after the `Command` has finished execution. Moving the
`TempDir` into the `current_dir` call would result in the `TempDir` being converted into
an internal representation, with the original value being dropped and the directory thus
being deleted, before the command can be executed.

The `touch` command would fail with an `No such file or directory` error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a temporary file and write some data into it:

```
use tempfile::tempfile;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file = tempfile()?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
```
Create a named temporary file and open an independent file handle:

```
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
use std::io::{Write, Read};
let text = "Brian was here. Briefly.";
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new()?;
// Re-open it.
let mut file2 = file1.reopen()?;
// Write some test data to the first handle.
file1.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
// Read the test data using the second handle.
let mut buf = String::new();
file2.read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
assert_eq!(buf, text);
```
Create a temporary directory and add a file to it:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let dir = tempdir()?;
let file_path = dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
let mut file = File::create(file_path)?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
// By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
// been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
// the directory will still be deleted when `dir` goes out
// of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
// succeeded.
drop(file);
dir.close()?;
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Create a new temporary file or directory with custom options.
- [Named](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)- Temp - File
- A named temporary file.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathPersistError.html)- Persist - Error
- Error returned when persisting a temporary file path fails.
- [Persist](https://docs.rs/struct.PersistError.html)- Error

- [Spooled](https://docs.rs/struct.SpooledTempFile.html)- Temp - File

- [TempDir](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)
- A directory in the filesystem that is automatically deleted when it goes out of scope.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [spooled_](https://docs.rs/fn.spooled_tempfile.html)- tempfile
- Create a new `SpooledTempFile``spooled_tempfile_in`
- [spooled_](https://docs.rs/fn.spooled_tempfile_in.html)- tempfile_ - in
- Construct a new `SpooledTempFile``spooled_tempfile`
- [tempdir](https://docs.rs/fn.tempdir.html)
- Create a new temporary directory. Also see `tempdir_in`
- [tempdir_](https://docs.rs/fn.tempdir_in.html)- in

- [tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html)
- Create a new temporary file. Also see `tempfile_in`
- [tempfile_](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile_in.html)- in
- Create a new temporary file in the specified directory. Also see `tempfile`

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/diesel_migrations/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

---

- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/diesel_migrations/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

# embed_migrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel_migrations/macro.embed_migrations.html

`embed_migrations!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

You can optionally pass the path to the migrations directory to this macro. When left
unspecified, Diesel will search for the migrations directory in the same way that
Diesel CLI does. If specified, the path should be relative to the directory where `Cargo.toml`
resides.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use diesel_migrations::{embed_migrations, EmbeddedMigrations, MigrationHarness};
pub const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!("../../migrations/postgres");
fn run_migrations(connection: &mut impl MigrationHarness<DB>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>> {
    // This will run the necessary migrations.
    //
    // See the documentation for `MigrationHarness` for
    // all available methods.
    connection.run_pending_migrations(MIGRATIONS)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-rebuilds)Automatic rebuilds

Due to limitations in rusts proc-macro API there is currently no
way to signal that a specific proc macro should be rerun if some
external file changes/is added. This implies that `embed_migrations!`
cannot regenerate the list of embedded migrations if **only** the
migrations are changed. This limitation can be solved by adding a
custom `build.rs` file to your crate, such that the crate is rebuild
if the migration directory changes.

Add the following `build.rs` file to your project to fix the problem

```
fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/your/migration/dir/relative/to/your/Cargo.toml");
}
```

---

# FileBasedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel_migrations/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html

`pub struct FileBasedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system

A valid migration directory contains a sub folder per migration.
Each migration folder contains a `up.sql` file containing the migration itself
and a `down.sql` file containing the necessary SQL to revert the migration.
Additionally each folder can contain a `metadata.toml` file controlling how the
individual migration should be handled by the migration harness.

To embed an existing migration folder into the final binary see
[ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
# Directory Structure
- 20151219180527_create_users
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
- 20160107082941_create_posts
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
    - metadata.toml
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/up.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  hair_color VARCHAR
);
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/down.sql
DROP TABLE users;
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/up.sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  body TEXT
);
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/down.sql
DROP TABLE posts;
```
```
## 20160107082941_create_posts/metadata.toml
## specifies if a migration is executed inside a
## transaction or not. This configuration is optional
## by default all migrations are run in transactions.
##
## For certain types of migrations, like creating an
## index onto a existing column, it is required
## to set this to false
run_in_transaction = true
```

# EmbeddedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel_migrations/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html

`pub struct EmbeddedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

    ) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>> { ... }
[pending_migrations](https://docs.rs#method.pending_migrations)<S: [MigrationSource](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/trait.MigrationSource.html)<DB>>(
        &mut self,
        source: S,
    ) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>>>> { ... }
}## Expand description

A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

Apply a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::run](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.run) internally and record
that a specific migration version was executed afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the migration in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::revert](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-apple-darwin/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.revert) internally
and record that a specific migration version was reverted afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the revert in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/2.3.2/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

---

[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! Provides functions for maintaining database schema.
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! itself. Diesel's migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don't need to be
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! directory containing `Cargo.toml`.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! `up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! you use the timestamp of creation for the version.
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! For more information, consult the [`embed_migrations!`] macro.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! ## Transactions
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! in before the migration started.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! See [`FileBasedMigrations`] for a full example and an explanation of the
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! "cannot run inside a transaction block" error that certain database operations produce.
[46](https://docs.rs#46)
[47](https://docs.rs#47)mod embedded_migrations;
[48](https://docs.rs#48)mod errors;
[49](https://docs.rs#49)mod file_based_migrations;
[50](https://docs.rs#50)mod migration_harness;
[51](https://docs.rs#51)
[52](https://docs.rs#52)pub use crate::embedded_migrations::EmbeddedMigrations;
[53](https://docs.rs#53)pub use crate::file_based_migrations::FileBasedMigrations;
[54](https://docs.rs#54)pub use crate::migration_harness::{HarnessWithOutput, MigrationHarness};
[55](https://docs.rs#55)pub use migrations_macros::embed_migrations;
[56](https://docs.rs#56)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)#[doc(hidden)]
[58](https://docs.rs#58)pub use crate::embedded_migrations::{EmbeddedMigration, EmbeddedName};
[59](https://docs.rs#59)#[doc(hidden)]
[60](https://docs.rs#60)pub use crate::errors::MigrationError;
[61](https://docs.rs#61)#[doc(hidden)]
[62](https://docs.rs#62)pub use crate::file_based_migrations::TomlMetadataWrapper;

# embed_migrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel_migrations/macro.embed_migrations.html

`embed_migrations!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

You can optionally pass the path to the migrations directory to this macro. When left
unspecified, Diesel will search for the migrations directory in the same way that
Diesel CLI does. If specified, the path should be relative to the directory where `Cargo.toml`
resides.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use diesel_migrations::{embed_migrations, EmbeddedMigrations, MigrationHarness};
pub const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!("../../migrations/postgres");
fn run_migrations(connection: &mut impl MigrationHarness<DB>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>> {
    // This will run the necessary migrations.
    //
    // See the documentation for `MigrationHarness` for
    // all available methods.
    connection.run_pending_migrations(MIGRATIONS)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-rebuilds)Automatic rebuilds

Due to limitations in rusts proc-macro API there is currently no
way to signal that a specific proc macro should be rerun if some
external file changes/is added. This implies that `embed_migrations!`
cannot regenerate the list of embedded migrations if **only** the
migrations are changed. This limitation can be solved by adding a
custom `build.rs` file to your crate, such that the crate is rebuild
if the migration directory changes.

Add the following `build.rs` file to your project to fix the problem

```
fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/your/migration/dir/relative/to/your/Cargo.toml");
}
```

---

# FileBasedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel_migrations/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html

`pub struct FileBasedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system

A valid migration directory contains a sub folder per migration.
Each migration folder contains a `up.sql` file containing the migration itself
and a `down.sql` file containing the necessary SQL to revert the migration.
Additionally each folder can contain a `metadata.toml` file controlling how the
individual migration should be handled by the migration harness.

To embed an existing migration folder into the final binary see
[ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
# Directory Structure
- 20151219180527_create_users
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
- 20160107082941_create_posts
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
    - metadata.toml
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/up.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  hair_color VARCHAR
);
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/down.sql
DROP TABLE users;
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/up.sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  body TEXT
);
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/down.sql
DROP TABLE posts;
```
```
## 20160107082941_create_posts/metadata.toml
## specifies if a migration is executed inside a
## transaction or not. This configuration is optional
## by default all migrations are run in transactions.
##
## For certain types of migrations, like creating an
## index onto a existing column, it is required
## to set this to false
run_in_transaction = true
```

`downcast` into `Box<dyn ConcreteType>` where `ConcreteType` implements `Trait`.Converts

}## Expand description

A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#142-143)

#### fn [run_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.run_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Apply a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::run](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.run) internally and record
that a specific migration version was executed afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the migration in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)#### fn [revert_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.revert_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)

#### fn [revert_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.revert_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Revert a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::revert](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.revert) internally
and record that a specific migration version was reverted afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the revert in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/2.3.2/i686-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

---

# embed_migrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/macro.embed_migrations.html

`embed_migrations!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

You can optionally pass the path to the migrations directory to this macro. When left
unspecified, Diesel will search for the migrations directory in the same way that
Diesel CLI does. If specified, the path should be relative to the directory where `Cargo.toml`
resides.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use diesel_migrations::{embed_migrations, EmbeddedMigrations, MigrationHarness};
pub const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!("../../migrations/postgres");
fn run_migrations(connection: &mut impl MigrationHarness<DB>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>> {
    // This will run the necessary migrations.
    //
    // See the documentation for `MigrationHarness` for
    // all available methods.
    connection.run_pending_migrations(MIGRATIONS)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-rebuilds)Automatic rebuilds

Due to limitations in rusts proc-macro API there is currently no
way to signal that a specific proc macro should be rerun if some
external file changes/is added. This implies that `embed_migrations!`
cannot regenerate the list of embedded migrations if **only** the
migrations are changed. This limitation can be solved by adding a
custom `build.rs` file to your crate, such that the crate is rebuild
if the migration directory changes.

Add the following `build.rs` file to your project to fix the problem

```
fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/your/migration/dir/relative/to/your/Cargo.toml");
}
```

---

# FileBasedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html

`pub struct FileBasedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system

A valid migration directory contains a sub folder per migration.
Each migration folder contains a `up.sql` file containing the migration itself
and a `down.sql` file containing the necessary SQL to revert the migration.
Additionally each folder can contain a `metadata.toml` file controlling how the
individual migration should be handled by the migration harness.

To embed an existing migration folder into the final binary see
[ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
# Directory Structure
- 20151219180527_create_users
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
- 20160107082941_create_posts
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
    - metadata.toml
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/up.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  hair_color VARCHAR
);
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/down.sql
DROP TABLE users;
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/up.sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  body TEXT
);
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/down.sql
DROP TABLE posts;
```
```
## 20160107082941_create_posts/metadata.toml
## specifies if a migration is executed inside a
## transaction or not. This configuration is optional
## by default all migrations are run in transactions.
##
## For certain types of migrations, like creating an
## index onto a existing column, it is required
## to set this to false
run_in_transaction = true
```

This method looks in the current and all parent directories for a folder named
`migrations`

This method fails if no valid migration directory is found

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

`downcast` into `Rc<ConcreteType>` where `ConcreteType` implements `Trait`.[Source](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/i686-pc-windows-msvc/src/diesel/expression/functions/aggregate_expressions.rs.html#491)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-WindowExpressionMethods-for-T)### impl<T> [WindowExpressionMethods](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/i686-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/expression/functions/aggregate_expressions/trait.WindowExpressionMethods.html) for T

Apply a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::run](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/i686-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.run) internally and record
that a specific migration version was executed afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the migration in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

and record that a specific migration version was reverted afterwards.

metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/2.3.2/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/index.html

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

# embed_migrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/macro.embed_migrations.html

`embed_migrations!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

You can optionally pass the path to the migrations directory to this macro. When left
unspecified, Diesel will search for the migrations directory in the same way that
Diesel CLI does. If specified, the path should be relative to the directory where `Cargo.toml`
resides.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use diesel_migrations::{embed_migrations, EmbeddedMigrations, MigrationHarness};
pub const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!("../../migrations/postgres");
fn run_migrations(connection: &mut impl MigrationHarness<DB>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>> {
    // This will run the necessary migrations.
    //
    // See the documentation for `MigrationHarness` for
    // all available methods.
    connection.run_pending_migrations(MIGRATIONS)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-rebuilds)Automatic rebuilds

Due to limitations in rusts proc-macro API there is currently no
way to signal that a specific proc macro should be rerun if some
external file changes/is added. This implies that `embed_migrations!`
cannot regenerate the list of embedded migrations if **only** the
migrations are changed. This limitation can be solved by adding a
custom `build.rs` file to your crate, such that the crate is rebuild
if the migration directory changes.

Add the following `build.rs` file to your project to fix the problem

```
fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/your/migration/dir/relative/to/your/Cargo.toml");
}
```

# FileBasedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html

`pub struct FileBasedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system

A valid migration directory contains a sub folder per migration.
Each migration folder contains a `up.sql` file containing the migration itself
and a `down.sql` file containing the necessary SQL to revert the migration.
Additionally each folder can contain a `metadata.toml` file controlling how the
individual migration should be handled by the migration harness.

To embed an existing migration folder into the final binary see
[ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
# Directory Structure
- 20151219180527_create_users
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
- 20160107082941_create_posts
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
    - metadata.toml
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/up.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  hair_color VARCHAR
);
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/down.sql
DROP TABLE users;
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/up.sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  body TEXT
);
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/down.sql
DROP TABLE posts;
```
```
## 20160107082941_create_posts/metadata.toml
## specifies if a migration is executed inside a
## transaction or not. This configuration is optional
## by default all migrations are run in transactions.
##
## For certain types of migrations, like creating an
## index onto a existing column, it is required
## to set this to false
run_in_transaction = true
```

# HarnessWithOutput in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel_migrations/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html

`pub struct HarnessWithOutput<'a, C, W> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

}## Expand description

A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#142-143)#### fn [run_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.run_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#142-143)

#### fn [run_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.run_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Apply a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::run](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.run) internally and record
that a specific migration version was executed afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the migration in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)#### fn [revert_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.revert_migration)(

    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)

    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Revert a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::revert](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.revert) internally
and record that a specific migration version was reverted afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the revert in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

# diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/2.3.2/diesel_migrations/

## Expand description

Provides functions for maintaining database schema.

A database migration always provides procedures to update the schema, as well as to revert itself. Diesel’s migrations are versioned, and run in order. Diesel also takes care of tracking which migrations have already been run automatically. Your migrations don’t need to be idempotent, as Diesel will ensure no migration is run twice unless it has been reverted.

Migrations should be placed in a `/migrations` directory at the root of your project (the same
directory as `Cargo.toml`). When any of these functions are run, Diesel will search for the
migrations directory in the current directory and its parents, stopping when it finds the
directory containing `Cargo.toml`.

Individual migrations should be a folder containing two files, `up.sql` and `down.sql`.
`up.sql` will be used to run the migration, while `down.sql` will be used for reverting it. The
folder itself should have the structure `{version}_{migration_name}`. It is recommended that
you use the timestamp of creation for the version.

Migrations can either be run with the CLI or embedded into the compiled application
and executed with code, for example right after establishing a database connection.
For more information, consult the [ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html) macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#transactions)Transactions

By default, each migration runs inside its own transaction. This means a failing migration is automatically rolled back, leaving the database in the state it was in before the migration started.

You can disable this behaviour on a per-migration basis. For file-based migrations,
add a `metadata.toml` file to the migration folder with `run_in_transaction = false`.
See [ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) for a full example and an explanation of the
“cannot run inside a transaction block” error that certain database operations produce.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [embed_](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html)- migrations
- This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedMigrations.html)- Migrations
- A migration source that embeds migrations into the final binary
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html)- Based - Migrations
- A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system
- [Harness](https://docs.rs/struct.HarnessWithOutput.html)- With - Output
- A migration harness that writes messages into some output for each applied/reverted migration

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Migration](https://docs.rs/trait.MigrationHarness.html)- Harness
- A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

---

# embed_migrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/diesel_migrations/macro.embed_migrations.html

`embed_migrations!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

This macro will read your migrations at compile time, and create a constant value containing an embedded list of all your migrations as available at compile time. This is useful if you would like to use Diesel’s migration infrastructure, but want to ship a single executable file (such as for embedded applications). It can also be used to apply migrations to an in memory database (Diesel does this for its own test suite).

You can optionally pass the path to the migrations directory to this macro. When left
unspecified, Diesel will search for the migrations directory in the same way that
Diesel CLI does. If specified, the path should be relative to the directory where `Cargo.toml`
resides.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use diesel_migrations::{embed_migrations, EmbeddedMigrations, MigrationHarness};
pub const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!("../../migrations/postgres");
fn run_migrations(connection: &mut impl MigrationHarness<DB>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>> {
    // This will run the necessary migrations.
    //
    // See the documentation for `MigrationHarness` for
    // all available methods.
    connection.run_pending_migrations(MIGRATIONS)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#automatic-rebuilds)Automatic rebuilds

Due to limitations in rusts proc-macro API there is currently no
way to signal that a specific proc macro should be rerun if some
external file changes/is added. This implies that `embed_migrations!`
cannot regenerate the list of embedded migrations if **only** the
migrations are changed. This limitation can be solved by adding a
custom `build.rs` file to your crate, such that the crate is rebuild
if the migration directory changes.

Add the following `build.rs` file to your project to fix the problem

```
fn main() {
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=path/to/your/migration/dir/relative/to/your/Cargo.toml");
}
```

---

# FileBasedMigrations in diesel_migrations - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/diesel_migrations/latest/diesel_migrations/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html

`pub struct FileBasedMigrations { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A migration source based on a migration directory in the file system

A valid migration directory contains a sub folder per migration.
Each migration folder contains a `up.sql` file containing the migration itself
and a `down.sql` file containing the necessary SQL to revert the migration.
Additionally each folder can contain a `metadata.toml` file controlling how the
individual migration should be handled by the migration harness.

To embed an existing migration folder into the final binary see
[ embed_migrations!](https://docs.rs/macro.embed_migrations.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
# Directory Structure
- 20151219180527_create_users
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
- 20160107082941_create_posts
    - up.sql
    - down.sql
    - metadata.toml
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/up.sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  hair_color VARCHAR
);
```
```
-- 20151219180527_create_users/down.sql
DROP TABLE users;
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/up.sql
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  body TEXT
);
```
```
-- 20160107082941_create_posts/down.sql
DROP TABLE posts;
```
```
## 20160107082941_create_posts/metadata.toml
## specifies if a migration is executed inside a
## transaction or not. This configuration is optional
## by default all migrations are run in transactions.
##
## For certain types of migrations, like creating an
## index onto a existing column, it is required
## to set this to false
run_in_transaction = true
```

}## Expand description

A migration harness is an entity which applies migration to an existing database

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#142-143)#### fn [run_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.run_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#142-143)

#### fn [run_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.run_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Apply a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::run](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.run) internally and record
that a specific migration version was executed afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the migration in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)#### fn [revert_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.revert_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/diesel_migrations/migration_harness.rs.html#154-157)

#### fn [revert_migration](https://docs.rs#tymethod.revert_migration)(
    &mut self,
    migration: &dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[MigrationVersion](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/struct.MigrationVersion.html)<'static>>

Revert a single migration

Types implementing this trait should call [ Migration::revert](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html#tymethod.revert) internally
and record that a specific migration version was reverted afterwards.

The default implementation wraps the revert in a transaction when the migration
metadata reports `run_in_transaction = true` (the default). See
[ FileBasedMigrations](https://docs.rs/struct.FileBasedMigrations.html) to learn how to configure
this for a specific migration.

) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/type.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Migration](https://docs.rs/diesel/2.3.8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/diesel/migration/trait.Migration.html)<DB>>>>

Get a list of non applied migrations for a specific migration source

The returned migration list is sorted in ascending order by the individual version of each migration

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:
